top_story_title: Citrix NetScaler zero-days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 exploited in the wild, KEV due date 30 September
top_story_summary: Citrix has confirmed that CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway have been exploited in the wild. CISA added both to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 September 2026 with a remediation due date of 30 September 2026. Per the KEV entries, CVE-2026-88771 is an improper input validation flaw that could let an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary commands, and CVE-2026-88772 is an out-of-bounds memory issue that could allow remote code execution or denial of service. Unit 42 reports it is aware of possible zero-day activity against NetScaler devices.
top_actions: Inventory every NetScaler ADC and Gateway instance, including MPX, VPX, SDX and any decommissioned-but-still-reachable units, and record the running build per HA pair.

Patch to the fixed release named in the Citrix advisory - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as no fixed build is stated in the current reporting. Upgrade the HA secondary first, fail over, then the primary.
Remove NSIP, SNIP and the management GUI (/nsgui, NITRO API, SSH) from internet exposure; restrict management to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
After upgrading, kill all active ICA/Gateway sessions and revoke session cookies and tokens - assume session material was stolen pre-patch.
Rotate nsroot and all local admin passwords, LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS+ service-account credentials, NITRO API keys and the appliance's TLS certificates and keys.
executive_summary: Citrix NetScaler is the whole story this cycle: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are exploited in the wild, both added to CISA KEV on 27 September with a 30 September due date, and Citrix has confirmed eight new vulnerabilities in total.

Advisories came from the Netherlands, the US and the UK within a day of each other, after incident responders raised NetScaler Gateway on Saturday - patch, then terminate sessions and rotate every secret the appliance held.
No fixed build numbers appear in the current reporting; check the Citrix advisory for the fixed release for your branch before scheduling the change.

Two vendor AI-defence items: Palo Alto Networks is extending its NVIDIA collaboration to control AI agent access and activity, and Cisco is shipping AI-powered threat detection in the Secure Firewall 200 Series for branch sites.

AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is now producing real reports at volume (GitHub's Taskflow agents, 20+ Android app bugs), which argues for a days-not-months patch window on internet-facing appliances.
Four of nine collected items were dropped as off-topic: Android app bugs, a Chrome extension, an AI model evaluation and a general weekly roundup.
key_actions: **Citrix** — Identify all NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances from asset inventory with their running build per HA pair, including VPX instances on SDX and any forgotten test units.

**Citrix** — Apply the vendor fixed release to all units in the device group - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as none is stated in the reporting - secondary first, then fail over and patch the primary; verify config sync afterwards.

**Citrix** — Read the Citrix advisory for the full set of eight vulnerabilities and patch to the fixed release for your branch rather than triaging CVE by CVE - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Citrix** — Read the national advisories from the Dutch, US and UK agencies for the indicators and forensic triage steps they publish, and run them before closing the incident.
